cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Salary – a fixed regular payment made by an employer to an employee.

p.em: Example: She receives a very good monthly salary from her bank job.

cosy-blockquote.p: Free time ≠ busy time – time when you are not working and can relax ≠ time when you have many duties.

p.em: Example: During my free time I love reading books, but my busy time at work is very exhausting.

cosy-blockquote.p: To earn – to receive money in return for work or services.

p.em: Example: He works on Saturdays to earn some extra money.

cosy-blockquote.p: To spend – to give money to pay for goods or services.

p.em: Example: I try not to spend too much money on expensive coffee.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rich ≠ poor – having a lot of money ≠ having very little money.

p.em: Example: The rich businessman bought a yacht, while the poor student walked to school.

cosy-blockquote.p: Relaxed ≠ stressed – feeling calm and comfortable ≠ feeling worried, anxious, and tired.

p.em: Example: A long walk in the park makes me feel relaxed, but my desk job makes me stressed.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hobby – an activity done regularly in one's leisure time for pleasure.

p.em: Example: My favorite weekend hobby is playing tennis with my friends.

cosy-blockquote.p: Important – of great significance or value; necessary.

p.em: Example: Good health is much more important than a big house.

cosy-blockquote.p: Happiness – the state of feeling happy, joyful, and satisfied.

p.em: Example: Spending time with my family brings me genuine happiness.

cosy-blockquote.p: To afford – to have enough money to pay for something.

p.em: Example: I cannot afford to buy a new smartphone this month.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
A: A high salary pays for a comfortable apartment and delicious food. B: Having abundant free time allows you to sleep well and stay healthy.
★ Do you think a high salary makes life much easier?

A: Having a lot of free time keeps you away from toxic office stress. B: Being busy at work makes you feel active and productive.
★ How do you usually spend your precious free time?

A: Working hard to earn money builds a strong, disciplined character. B: Having free hours lets you learn new skills at your own pace.
★ Do you have to work on weekends to earn extra money?

A: Having money to spend on luxury travel is very exciting. B: Free time lets you enjoy simple pleasures like walking in nature.
★ Do you prefer to spend your money or save it for the future?

A: A rich lifestyle offers absolute safety and high-quality healthcare. B: A simple, quiet life prevents complicated social anxieties.
★ Do you wish to be very rich, or do you prefer a simple life?

A: Feeling relaxed during a long morning walk is beautiful. B: A busy schedule keeps your mind sharp and highly focused.
★ Do you feel completely relaxed when you are at home alone?

A: Having a creative hobby like painting brings great joy. B: Earning a bonus at work is extremely satisfying.
★ What is your favorite creative hobby today?

A: A high salary is important to support your children. B: Free hours are important to play and talk with your kids.
★ Is a big bank account the most important thing for you?

A: Real happiness comes from feeling calm and relaxed. B: Buying nice gifts for friends brings wonderful shared joy.
★ What brings you more happiness: buying a product or sleeping?

A: Having money to afford good books and classes is great. B: Free hours are necessary to actually read the books you buy.
★ What is one expensive thing you want to afford soon?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
A: A low salary can create intense survival anxiety. B: Having too much free time can make you feel lazy.
★ Have you ever had a job with a very low salary?

A: A lack of free time leads to rapid burnout and stress. B: Infinite free hours can make your life feel empty.
★ Does a completely empty weekend ever make you feel bored?

A: Having no way to earn money makes you dependent on others. B: Earning money often requires working in toxic offices.
★ Have you ever had a very stressful boss?

A: Having no money to spend stops you from enjoying the city. B: Spending too much money makes you regret your actions.
★ Do you regret some of your past shopping purchases?

A: A poor person struggles to afford basic necessities. B: A rich lifestyle can make you highly materialistic.
★ Do you worry about becoming too materialistic?

A: A highly stressed manager is very difficult to work with. B: A completely relaxed schedule can make you lose focus.
★ What is the most stressed moment of your week?

A: An expensive hobby can ruin your monthly savings. B: Having no hobby makes your weekends feel very dry.
★ Is tennis or skiing considered an expensive hobby in your town?

A: Sacrificing family time for an important meeting is painful. B: Having no important goals can make you feel lost.
★ What is the most important goal of your life right now?

A: True happiness is impossible when you are constantly tired. B: Possessions bring only a temporary wave of happiness.
★ What is the simplest thing that brings you genuine happiness?

A: If you cannot afford rent, you will feel extreme anxiety. B: Affording luxury items can alienate you from simple friends.
★ Do you think luxury clothes make people look arrogant?

ul.li: Incorrect: Free time is more important than money → Correct: Free time is more important than money ((For long adjectives like 'important', use 'more important than', not 'importanter'))
Incorrect: He work very hard to earn money → Correct: He works very hard to earn money ((Third-person singular 's' is required for verbs in the present simple))
Incorrect: I cannot afford to buy a car → Correct: I cannot afford to buy a car ((The verb 'afford' is followed by a to-infinitive))
